title: reviewer output
description: Canonical machine-readable output contract for the reviewer role. See agents/reviewer.md Step 5 for the prose contract this mirrors.

buildFailing.description: Optional. true when the project's build or test suite FAILS on the branch under review. On a CHANGES_NEEDED verdict the orchestrator guarantees a fix is dispatched: if none of your reopenIds can be reopened and no in-goal newTask covers it, it files an in-goal fix task carrying your notes. Omit or false when the build and tests pass.

title.description: Plain text only: letters, digits, space, and . , : ; ! ? ( ) ' _ / [ ] - -- nothing else. No backticks, double quotes, $, or backslash (the title is interpolated into a shell command downstream). Do NOT wrap a command/flag/filename in backticks here -- write it plain (e.g. "Surface the service registration mode in the status output") or move the formatted detail into description instead, which has no such restriction. NOT enforced as a hard schema constraint here (deliberately no "pattern"): a single out-of-allowlist newTask title must never make ajv reject/retry the WHOLE structured verdict (verdict, notes, reopenIds, and the other newTasks) -- see validateNewTask() in fleet-sprint/runner.js, the actual (per-item, non-fatal) enforcement point, applied after parsing.

kb_promotions.description: Entries this reviewer VERIFIED against the tree and is promoting to CONFIRMED. Reviewer-only: promotion is the sole path that mints CONFIRMED, and widening capture does not widen promotion. The engine makes the kb_promote calls.

id.description: The entry id, copied verbatim from the 'KNOWLEDGE BANK -- promotion candidates' block in your dispatch prompt. That block is the ONLY source of promotable ids -- do not call a kb_* tool to find one, and never invent one.

reason.description: The evidence for this promotion -- what you actually checked. kb_promote refuses a trivial reason.

kb_discards.description: Promotion candidates this reviewer showed to be WRONG and is discarding (the entry drops out of every later read). Reviewer-only, with the same evidence bar as kb_promotions. An id may appear in at most one of kb_promotions, kb_discards and kb_rejects -- the engine refuses duplicates. The engine makes the discard calls.

id.description: The entry id, copied verbatim from the 'KNOWLEDGE BANK -- promotion candidates' block in your dispatch prompt. That block is the ONLY source of discardable ids -- do not call a kb_* tool to find one, and never invent one.

reason.description: The evidence that the entry is wrong -- what you actually checked that contradicts its claim.

kb_rejects.description: Promotion candidates that are TRUE but fail the capture rubric, or are self-contradicting, garbled or mix several claims. Reviewer-only. An id may not appear in more than one of kb_promotions, kb_discards and kb_rejects. The engine retires them with the reason.

id.description: The entry id, copied verbatim from the 'KNOWLEDGE BANK -- promotion candidates' block in your dispatch prompt. That block is the ONLY source of rejectable ids -- do not call a kb_* tool to find one, and never invent one.

reason.description: Why the entry fails the capture rubric or is unusable (contradicting, garbled, multi-claim) -- what you actually checked.

kb_captures.description: Durable knowledge this role verified during its run. The engine makes the kb_capture calls; the role only decides. Optional -- omit or send [] to capture nothing.

items.description: One capture. Everything listed under each field is checked by the engine per capture, never by the report schema: a capture that breaks a rule is refused and logged on its own, and the rest of this report stands. See the capture rubric.

type.description: REQUIRED string, one of: knowledge, learning, runbook.

title.description: REQUIRED string, 8 to 160 characters, ASCII only.

summary.description: REQUIRED string, 20 to 500 characters, ASCII only. The lesson in at most 2 sentences, present tense, standing alone as current truth.

trigger.description: REQUIRED string, exactly one of the listed examples: what kind of event produced this lesson. Never "describes the change".

content.description: Optional string, 40 to 2000 characters, ASCII only. Written only when it adds what the summary cannot hold (labelled sections: Context, Symptom, Cause, Rule/Fix, Tried (failed), Evidence). Content that repeats the summary is refused. A failed-attempt capture must have Cause and Rule/Fix. No credentials or token-shaped strings.

source_files.description: REQUIRED array of strings, at least one: files that make this claim checkable. An entry with no basis is rejected, because the freshness sweep can never stale it.

symbols.description: Optional array of strings: symbols this claim is about.

recall_cues.description: Optional array of strings: phrases a future reader would search for to find this lesson.

error_signatures.description: Optional array of strings: exact error strings that this lesson explains.

toolUse.description: How this run used the kb_* and code_* tools its role prompt expects (Step 0). Optional for backward compatibility, but expected: report "unavailable" or "not_needed" with a note rather than skipping the calls silently.

kb.description: used = kb_query was called (kb_session_prime alone is not used).

code.description: used = code_impact, code_context or code_graph was called.

note.description: Why a value is not "used": which tool was missing or failed, or why no lookup was needed.

kb_used.description: Optional. Knowledge bank entries (pushed into your prompt or returned by a query) you actually relied on, and how. Omit or send [] when none. Each item is checked by the engine, never by the report schema: a malformed item is logged and dropped, and the rest of this report stands.

items.description: One entry used: an object {id, how}.

id.description: REQUIRED string: the KB entry id exactly as it was given to you.

how.description: REQUIRED string: one sentence on how the entry shaped your work.

kb_wrong.description: Optional. Knowledge bank entries that proved wrong in practice. The engine forwards each one as KB feedback. Omit or send [] when none. Each item is checked by the engine, never by the report schema: a malformed item is logged and dropped, and the rest of this report stands.

items.description: One wrong entry: an object {id, reason}.

id.description: REQUIRED string: the KB entry id exactly as it was given to you.

reason.description: REQUIRED string: what was wrong, as observed.
